newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds up, unaffected by political events.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds up, unaffected by political events.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed up on Wednesday and were unaffected by political events with gains across the board except for dollar-linked bonds, traders said.
* Consumer price index (CPI) linked government bonds: +0.3 pct to 167.87
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for 4 years): +0.1 pct to 164.95
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 to 157.16
"Political events have less effect on the bond market because there are hardly any foreign investors in the market," said an analyst at Sahar Securities.

U.S. President Bill Clinton has convened a two-day summit to defuse tensions between Israelis and Palestinians. Five days of clashes that killed 72 people erupted after Israel opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

The analyst at Sahar said the rally in CPI-linked bonds which has characterised trading in the last few days was due mainly to the fact that provident funds have started reinvesting in bonds and because the government was issuing less CPI-linked bonds.
"Provident funds find they had overly pessimistic estimates of redemptions and now have excess liquidity which they are reinvesting in the bond market," he said.

Prices of dollar-linked bonds fell on estimates the dollar would continue to decline in coming days, traders said. The Israeli shekel rose on Wednesday and the central bank bought dollars to stop its appreciation.
Meiron Katzap of Batucha Securities said the rises in the Makams were due to expectations for a low CPI in September.
September's CPI will be published on October 15. The unlinked shekel bonds were also up on Wednesday.

Notes: Provident funds, long-term savings funds with tax benefits, had been dumping bonds to meet massive public redemptions. To stop the falling bond prices the central bank has bought government bonds.
Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
